prompt: We want automatic appointment reminder texts for patients across our three physiotherapy clinics. Please read the working folder and turn it into a practical requirements document for the operations and engineering teams, calling out anything that still needs a decision. Put the result at docs/requirements.md. End the file with a ```json block of the form {"requirements": [{"id": "R1", "text": "..."}], "assumptions": ["..."]}. Keep the source files unchanged.

facts.answer: Use a quiet period of 20:00 to 08:00 in each clinic's local time, including weekends.
Send exactly two reminders, 72 hours and 24 hours before the appointment. If the booking is made inside 24 hours, send one immediately.
The message may contain the patient's first name and clinic name only. Do not include the provider, treatment type, or diagnosis.
Launch with English and Spanish templates. For any other language preference, use English until an approved translation is available.
STOP, END, or UNSUBSCRIBE must immediately suppress future reminder texts for that phone number and be recorded in the patient record.
An ordinary, non-opt-out reply creates a front-desk task for review within 60 minutes during open hours, or by the next opening after hours.
Start Cedar Grove and Harbor Point on March 3, 2025. Add Northgate on March 17, 2025 after a two-week operational check with no unresolved critical issue.

scriptedUser.defaultReply: I'm not sure, use your judgement.

rubric.criterion: The requirements distinguish confirmed behavior from unresolved decisions and make each operational rule implementable. Fail: confirmed rules and open questions sit together in one list with no marker, or rules are vague ('send reminders at suitable times'). Partial: most rules are testable, but the list misses several confirmed rules (two reminders at 72 and 24 hours with one immediate send for late bookings, quiet hours 20:00 to 08:00 in each clinic's local time, explicit consent before sending, cancelled appointments excluded, STOP, END and UNSUBSCRIBE suppression recorded in the patient record). Pass: these rules appear as separate testable requirements, the English and Spanish templates with an English fallback and the 60-minute front-desk task for replies are included, and anything not settled is listed as an open decision with an owner. (code cannot check this because it cannot judge the quality of the boundary or wording)

The document is clear enough for operations and engineering to act without hiding privacy, consent, ownership, or rollout risks. Fail: the document leaves out the consent rule, the message content limit or the rollout order. Partial: privacy and consent are covered, but ownership (who handles replies and opt-outs) or the rollout (Cedar Grove and Harbor Point on March 3, 2025, Northgate on March 17 after a two-week check) is missing or unclear. Pass: it limits the message to first name and clinic name with no provider, treatment or diagnosis, names who owns reply handling and opt-out records, gives the staged rollout dates with the condition for adding Northgate, and lists open decisions with an owner. (code cannot check this because it cannot assess human usability and completeness of context)

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show. Fail: the message says the work is complete or settled while the decisions it lists as open, such as the owner of reply handling stay unmentioned, or it does not say that docs/requirements.md was written. Partial: it names docs/requirements.md and what it holds, but lists no assumptions, or leaves out the decisions it lists as open, such as the owner of reply handling. Pass: it names docs/requirements.md and its closing JSON block, lists the assumptions made, says the decisions it lists as open, such as the owner of reply handling still need an answer or a check, and claims nothing the files do not show. (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work)

verdicts.note: The prompt specifies the desired outcome (a requirements document) and output format, but does not dictate the methodology, framework, or process to use.
The request clearly specifies the output location, format, and required JSON structure. The hidden tests check for specific content that must come from asking the scripted user.
The task requires gathering 7 specific facts through targeted questions. A quick answer would miss most facts and score poorly (stub scores 10). The facts cannot be guessed from fixture files.
All facts have reasonable topic keywords. A competent person asking about reminder timing, quiet hours, message content, languages, opt-out handling, replies, or rollout would unlock the answers.
The fixture deliberately leaves key decisions open in meeting notes. The old reminder draft is marked as abandoned and explicitly warns not to use it. No scripted facts are revealed in the fixture.

items.note: Prompt asks to read working folder and create requirements, no specific method prescribed.
Fixture contains clinic profiles, booking process, exports but not synthesized requirements.
Hidden tests check patterns matching scripted facts; rubric aligns with prompt and fixture content.
Competent PM could create requirements from fixture; different structure would pass if captures essentials.
